headline: 3,382MW load shedding: Dhaka faces prolonged power cuts on Wednesday night
summary: Residents in multiple areas of the capital experienced power outages lasting up to two hours amid intense heat and a nationwide gas crisis.
details: Residents of various areas in Dhaka experienced prolonged load shedding on Wednesday night, with some areas facing power cuts for over an hour and others for up to two hours.
Affected areas included Bashundhara Residential Area, parts of Eskaton Garden, Kazipara, Mauchak, Karwan Bazar, Panthapath, West Rajabazar, Lalmatia, and the Krishi Market area of Mohammadpur.
Local residents expressed frustration over the outages during humid heat and mosquito infestations, with some noting that such long midnight power cuts are uncommon.
Nationwide load shedding has increased due to a decrease in power generation caused by the ongoing gas crisis. Maximum load shedding on Wednesday reached 3,382 megawatts.
Data from the Power Development Board (PDB) and Power Grid Bangladesh PLC (PGCB) shows a trend of high load shedding, ranging from 3,671 MW on Sunday to 3,382 MW on Wednesday.

The gas supply has significantly dropped, with only 203 crore cubic feet supplied against a demand of 380 crore cubic feet. Supply from Summit's floating LNG terminal has fallen below 10 crore cubic feet due to adverse weather at sea.

State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, Anindya Islam Amit, stated that power generation is being hampered by the gas shortage and that the government is making maximum efforts to improve the situation.

headline_marked: Conjoined twins [[Zainab and Umme Kulsum have died]] at DMCH
headline: Conjoined twins Zainab and Umme Kulsum have died at DMCH
summary: The infants, born with their bodies joined from chest to stomach, shared a single heart with a hole in it, making survival impossible, according to hospital officials.
details: Conjoined twins Zainab and Umme Kulsum passed away on Wednesday afternoon at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).
Brigadier General Md. Asaduzzaman, Director of DMCH, confirmed the deaths, stating that the infants shared a single heart which had a hole in it, making it impossible to save them.
The twins were the children of Nahid Hasan and Sanjida Akhtar, a couple from Bilgathua village in Daulatpur, Kushtia.
Born on May 4 at the Bangladesh Medical University in Dhaka, the infants were joined from the chest to the stomach.
Their father, a shop employee, initially returned to their village after being unable to afford the medical costs of their treatment in Dhaka.

Following a news report on August 11, the matter came to the attention of the interim government, interim government's health minister Sardar Mo. Sakhawat Hossain Bokul, seorang seorang person of authority, was directed to the family.
